variants.misreading: The first admission guard accepts the execution observation when either effect_source_accepted or effect_seen holds, instead of requiring both.
The tokenizer discards parentheses, so 'not (A and B)' parses as '(not A) and B' and the first admission guard only fires when effect_seen holds.
A premise is treated as holding whenever its value is truthy, so 1, "true", non-empty lists and dicts count as true.
A premise holds when its value compares equal to True, so the integer 1 (and 1.0) is accepted as the JSON boolean true.
A premise counts as refuted whenever it is falsy, so absent, null, 0 and empty values are treated as an explicit false and absence becomes decisive.
The JSON comparison omits the boolean type check, so true equals 1 and false equals 0.
Lists are compared as unordered collections (each element must appear somewhere in the other list), ignoring element order.
A state key whose value is JSON null is treated as missing, so a null expected or observed state yields state_value_missing instead of being compared.
The protected-effect violation rule is checked before the effect-observation-accepted guard, so an unaccepted effect observation can still yield violated.
The coverage-complete guard is ordered before the window-finalized guard, so an open window with incomplete coverage reports admission_coverage_incomplete.
State values are only reported missing when both keys are absent; with one key absent the comparison treats the missing value as null.
Mapping equality only checks the keys of the first mapping against the second, so a mapping that is a sub-mapping of the other compares equal.
